chapter: Family follow-ups from the first reels
title: Maternal grandmother's college and the Walton family in Denison
summary: Grandmother's liberal arts education, the Walton School in Rock Hill, uncles and their hunting dogs.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You mentioned before on the other tapes that your maternal grandmother was fortunate enough to have a college education. Where was it she went to college?
And she had studied some music there?
Well, she -- I imagine she had a liberal arts type of education, which usually, in those days, if no more than anything, was music appreciation.
Would you know, were there very many
female students there, or was it (inaudible) --
(Inaudible) relation to the number of male students?
There were quite a few female students that were ______ at that time, in relation to men students.
You also mentioned the Walton School, which was (inaudible) school. Was that (inaudible)?

Dennison, Texas. It was located in the section of Dennison that was known as Rock Hill and as a matter of fact, a whole lot of people that you might know came from Rock Hill, like President Eisenhower. He used to be down there and he used to borrow some of my uncle's dogs to hunt with when (unintelligible). They were pecan pickers.

Well, there were three of them and they were all hunters. They had some of the best hunting dogs around. The kids raised the hunting dogs and my grandfather raised the race horses and they had coon dogs that they hunted the coons with and they had greyhounds that they cours ed the rabbits with and they had pointers and setters, Irish setters, that they used to use for quail and pheasant, grouse.

Oh, William, Patrick, Patrick David, and Robert Walton, all Waltons. One of them is still living. He's my favorite uncle. I visit with him every week. That's Bill, my mother's youngest brother. He's the only one left out of the family now.
